result:
In upstream proxy mode, the CONNECT authority now brackets IPv6 literals, so a target of `::1` port 443 gives `[::1]:443`. I didn't run any tests, and I didn't add one.

The change is in `HttpUpstreamProxy.start_handshake` in `mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`. It checks the host with `ipaddress.ip_address` and wraps it in `[...]` only when it is IPv6. Hostnames and IPv4 addresses are unchanged. The same authority is used for the `Host` header when `http_connect_send_host_header` is on, so that header is bracketed too.

I didn't confirm that `.encode("idna")` passes the bracketed host through unchanged. I expect it does, because the bracketed string is pure ASCII.

The natural test would be a case in `test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py`, next to the existing upstream-proxy CONNECT tests, that expects `CONNECT [::1]:443`.
